pcs.pc_description: Regularly inspect, troubleshoot, and maintain all machinery and equipment involved in hydrogen production, storage, and distribution.

Perform preventive maintenance tasks to minimize downtime and ensure equipment reliability, implementing predictive maintenance strategies using data analysis and monitoring tools to address potential issues proactively.
Conduct routine maintenance on electrolyzers for peak efficiency, monitoring and troubleshooting performance, including membrane degradation, gas leaks, and electrode fouling.
Coordinate with manufacturers or suppliers for specialized maintenance or component replacements.

Execute maintenance tasks on chemical equipment, pumps, valves, air compressors, water treatment RO’s, fans, vessels, and buildings, including routine inspections, lubrication, and maintenance of hydrogen compressors, valves, seals, and pipeline.
Perform regular inspections of hydrogen storage equipment for integrity, safety valves, and instrumentation.
Conduct maintenance on cryogenic components, heat exchangers, and equipment in liquefaction units.
Participate in troubleshooting efforts to identify and resolve equipment malfunctions, working closely with other maintenance personnel to diagnose and address complex issues.
Stay updated on maintenance best practices and technologies, participating in training programs to enhance skills and knowledge.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the reliability and efficiency of maintenance processes, providing feedback on procedures and suggesting improvements.
Coordinate with other maintenance personnel to plan and execute scheduled maintenance activities, while also offering input on equipment performance and reliability for maintenance planning.
Adhere to and enforce strict safety protocols to ensure a safe working environment for all personnel, including the proper use of PPE.
Conduct safety inspections and participate in training programs, responding promptly to emergencies and incidents, taking appropriate actions to mitigate risks.
Perform routine inspections and maintenance on the emergency diesel generator.
Operate facility mobile equipment and perform routine inspections and maintenance.
Support safety and environmental standards, inspections, and testing.
Participate in emergency response drills and be prepared to respond to incidents involving the release or handling of hydrogen, implementing emergency shutdown procedures when necessary.
Monitor and respond to gas detection alarms, ensuring proper ventilation in case of gas releases.
Calibrate and test mechanical equipment to maintain accurate and efficient operations.
Monitor and analyze data from various sensors to identify deviations and address potential problems.
Diagnose and troubleshoot technical issues related to electrolyzers and other equipment to minimize downtime and production interruptions.

Collaborate with other departments to identify root causes of problems and implement effective solutions. Conduct root cause analysis for equipment failures or process deviations, identifying and addressing underlying issues to prevent future occurrences.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including inspections, repairs, and equipment modifications.
Update and review documentation related to equipment manuals, procedures, and safety guidelines.
Work closely with engineers, operations teams, and other stakeholders to optimize plant performance, collaborating on projects aimed at improving efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing safety.
Identify opportunities for process improvement and efficiency enhancements.
Implement and optimize predictive maintenance programs to maximize equipment reliability and lifespan.
Maintain accurate logs and records of operational parameters, events, and maintenance activities
Generating reports on equipment performance, incidents, and production metrics.
